headline: Near-complete phased genomes expose centromere variation and hidden East Asian diversity
label: Human Pangenome Resource Development
summary: Near-complete phased assemblies now resolve centromeres and population-specific sequence at scale, extending pangenome reference beyond linear genomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the move from single linear references toward dense, phased, near-complete genome assemblies that resolve sequence at higher completeness. One preprint assembles 6,312 complete human centromeres from 320 phased genomes, mapping HOR arrays, pericentric inversions, kinetochore sites and population stratification. A second releases 320 near-complete, phased East Asian assemblies from 160 individuals, reporting novel sequences, gene gains, structural variants and inversions. What is new is that centromere-level variation is analysed as a population-structure question, not only as a per-genome feature. A published nucDetective benchmark on Plasmodium falciparum MNase-seq is methodologically distinct, addressing nucleosome arrays and promoter architecture rather than human assembly.
